name: doclap/faq-list
title: FAQ list
description: An editable, filterable frequently asked questions surface.

asideCopy.default: Open each question to see the details.

default.question: What should I prepare before reaching out?
default.answer: Just your goals, context and a few things you want to change. If you already have a brief, guidelines or a current website, bring them into the conversation.

default.question: Can we start before the idea is clear?
default.answer: Yes. The first step is clarifying the problem, the audience and the success criteria before agreeing on the design scope.

default.question: What steps does a project go through?
default.answer: Listen and define scope → build the creative direction → design and prototype → develop, test and hand over. Feedback milestones are agreed per project.

default.question: Can I be involved in the design process?
default.answer: Yes. Contextual feedback makes a project better. We will agree on the decision-maker, review timing and how feedback is consolidated so the process stays clear.

default.question: Do you support mobile design and accessibility?
default.answer: Responsive behaviour, readability, keyboard operation, focus states and reduced-motion options are all part of design and testing. The specific standard scope is agreed in the brief.

default.question: What do cost and timeline look like?
default.answer: No fixed pricing or timeline has been published. Both depend on scope, number of screens, level of interaction and technical requirements. They need to be confirmed before we start.

default.question: Can we collaborate on motion or development only?
default.answer: We can agree on a standalone scope for design, motion or creative development. I will first check how well it fits your existing system before proposing an approach.

default.question: What do I receive after handover?
default.answer: The list of design files, source code, assets, documentation and post-handover support should be defined within the project scope. Nothing unagreed is assumed by default.

default.question: Does animation slow a website down?
default.answer: It can, if used without intent. I favour transform and opacity, limit heavy assets, stop rendering when it is not needed, and always provide reduced-motion options or a fallback.

default.question: Do the contact form and newsletter send yet?
default.answer: Not yet. This is a prototype. The contact form can save a draft or download a brief on your device; no email is connected. The home newsletter is not connected to a mailing service either.
